1: # RS-Agent Bot Guide
2: 
3: You're here to play the mmo game through the progressive development of botting scripts, starting small then adapting to your desires and ideas.
4: It is strongly recommended to get started and make the first step towards your goals, then researching and learning as you go.
5: 
6: ## First Time Setup
7: 
8: **Create a new bot using the setup script:**
9: 
10: Ask the user for a bot name (max 12 chars, alphanumeric). If they skip, use the command without a username to auto-generate a random 9-character name.
11: 
12: ```bash
13: # With custom username
14: bun bots/create-bot.ts {username}
15: 
16: # Auto-generate random username
17: bun bots/create-bot.ts
18: 
19: # Use local server (sets SERVER=localhost in bot.env)
20: bun bots/create-bot.ts {username} --local
21: 
22: # Use a custom server
23: bun bots/create-bot.ts {username} --server=myserver.example.com
24: ```
25: 
26: This automatically creates:
27: 
28: - `bots/{username}/bot.env` - Credentials with auto-generated password
29: - `bots/{username}/lab_log.md` - Session notes template
30: - `bots/{username}/script.ts` - Ready-to-run starter script
31: 
32: ### Start a Game Client (scripts only)
33: 
34: Scripts (`bun bots/{username}/*.ts`) and `bun sdk/cli.ts` need a running game
35: client; they never start one. Before running a script, start the headless lite
36: client in the background and leave it running:
37: 
38: ```bash
39: cd server/webclient && bun install && bun src/lite/runner.ts {username}
40: ```
41: 
42: It logs `Gateway connected, registering as '{username}'` once it's ready. One
43: process per bot; it exits non-zero if the game session ends. Without it, a
44: script exits with `No game client is attached`. MCP `execute_code` doesn't need
45: this step; it opens a browser client itself.
46: 
47: ### Quick Start
48: 
49: 1. Install dependencies: `bun install` (from project root)
50: 2. Open project in your AI coding tool — the MCP server will be available automatically
51: 3. Control your bot with suggestions.
52: 
53: ### Tools
54: 
55: | Tool                           | Description                                    |
56: | ------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------- |
57: | `execute_code(bot_name, code)` | Run code on a bot. Auto-connects on first use. |
58: | `list_bots()`                  | List connected bots                            |
59: | `disconnect_bot(name)`         | Disconnect a bot                               |
60: 
61: ### Example
62: 
63: ```typescript
64: // Just execute - auto-connects on first use
65: execute_code({
66:   bot_name: "mybot",
67:   code: `
68:     const state = sdk.getState();
69:     console.log('Position:', state.player.worldX, state.player.worldZ);
70: 
71:     // Chop trees for 1 minute
72:     const endTime = Date.now() + 60_000;
73:     while (Date.now() < endTime) {
74:       const tree = sdk.findNearbyLoc(/^tree$/i);
75:       if (tree) await bot.chopTree(tree);
76:     }
77: 
78:     return sdk.getInventory();
79:   `,
80: });
81: ```
82: 
83: See `mcp/README.md` for detailed API reference.
84: 
85: Code runs in an async context with `bot` (BotActions) and `sdk` (BotSDK) available as globals.
86: 
87: ## Reporting SDK Bugs
88: 
89: When the SDK has a bug or rough edge, first find a workaround, then file a report. One command, no auth, no permission needed:
90: 
91: ```bash
92: bun sdk/bug-report.ts "incorrect results from bot.foo(), had to use raw sdk.sendFoo() instead for xyz reason."
93: ```
94: 
95: Important note: The game itself is extremely well tested and complete, it's not buggy. If you can't figure out how to do something, don't blame the game, blame your assumptions and keep investigating. File a bug report _after_ you figure out
96: what's going on, don't just assume the game is broken because you got confused, and give up. The SDK is a thin layer on top of the game, and the game is the source of truth.
97: 
98: After filing the bug, keep working on your goal!
99: 
100: ## Session Workflow
101: 
102: This is a **persistent character** - you don't restart fresh each time. The workflow is:
103: 
104: ### 1. Check World State First
105: 
106: Before writing any script, check where the bot is and what it has:
107: 
108: ```bash
109: bun sdk/cli.ts {username}
110: ```
111: 
112: This shows: position, inventory, skills, nearby NPCs/objects, and more.
113: 
114: **Exception**: Skip this if you just created the character and know it's at spawn.
115: 
116: **Tutorial Check**: If the character is in the tutorial area, call `await bot.skipTutorial()` before running any other scripts. The tutorial blocks normal gameplay.
117: 
118: ### 2. Write Your Script
119: 
120: Edit `bots/{username}/script_name.ts` with your goal. Keep scripts focused on one task. you may write multiple scripts for different tasks and switch between them.
121: 
122: ### 3. Run the Script
123: 
124: ```bash
125: bun bots/{username}/script_name.ts
126: ```
127: 
128: ### 4. Observe and Iterate
129: 
130: Watch the output. After the script finishes (or fails), check state again:
131: 
132: ```bash
133: bun sdk/cli.ts {username}
134: ```
135: 
136: Record observations in `lab_log.md`, then improve the script.
137: 
138: ### Chatting Without Taking Control
139: 
140: To talk in-game (or read chat) without disturbing whatever script currently
141: owns the bot, use the chat CLI — it connects in `observe` mode, which can send
142: chat (and nothing else) and never pre-empts (or gets pre-empted by) a
143: controller:
144: 
145: ```bash
146: bun sdk/chat.ts {username} "meet me at the bank"   # send public chat
147: bun sdk/chat.ts {username} --to {player} "on my way"  # send a private message
148: bun sdk/chat.ts {username}                          # recent chat
149: bun sdk/chat.ts {username} --watch                  # tail live
150: ```
151: 
152: Public chat is capped at 400 chars per message; `sdk.say()` auto-splits longer
153: text into wire-safe chunks.
154: 
155: Private messages (`sdk.dm(name, text)` / `sdk.sendPrivateMessage(name, msg)`)
156: reach the target anywhere in the world - no friends-list setup needed - and
157: show up in `getChat()` as type 3 (received) / 6 (sent). The server accepts one
158: social packet (say or PM) per tick; `dm()` paces its chunks automatically.
159: 
160: ## Script Duration Guidelines
161: 
162: **Start short, extend as you gain confidence:**
163: 
164: | Duration      | Use When                                              |
165: | ------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
166: | **10s**       | New script, single actions, untested logic, debugging |
167: | **30s-1 min** | Validated approach, building confidence               |
168: | **5+ min**    | Proven strategy, grinding runs. USE SPARINGLY         |
169: 
170: A failed 5-minute run wastes more time than five 30 second diagnostic runs. **Fail fast and start simple.**
171: 
172: Look out for "I can't reach" messages - the solution is often to open closed gates or that the item isn't accessible.
173: 
174: Read and grep in the learnings/ and wiki/ folder for tips, skill guides, item and npc locations, and shop information.
175: 
176: ## SDK API Reference
177: 
178: For the complete method reference, see **[sdk/API.md](sdk/API.md)** (auto-generated from source).
179: 
180: **Quick overview:**
181: 
182: - `bot.*` - High-level actions that attempt to observe method-specific evidence (chopTree, walkTo, attack, etc.). Check a result when the method returns one.
183: - `sdk.*` - State queries and low-level browser-client dispatches. A successful `send*` result does not prove the game server applied the effect.
184: 
185: ### bot.\* Quick Reference
186: 
187: | Method                          | What it does                                                     |
188: | ------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
189: | `walkTo(x, z, tolerance?)`      | Pathfind to coords, opens doors along the way                    |
190: | `talkTo(target)`                | Walk to NPC, start dialog                                        |
191: | `interactNpc(target, option?)`  | Walk to NPC, interact with any option (e.g. `'trade'`, `'fish'`) |
192: | `interactLoc(target, option?)`  | Walk to loc, interact with any option (e.g. `'mine'`, `'smelt'`) |
193: | `attack(target)`                | Walk to an NPC or player and start combat                    |
194: | `castSpell(target, spell)`      | Cast a combat spell on an NPC or player                         |
195: | `pickpocketNpc(target)`         | Pickpocket NPC, detects XP gain vs stun                          |
196: | `chopTree(target?)`             | Chop tree, wait for logs                                         |
197: | `pickupItem(target)`            | Pick up ground item                                              |
198: | `openDoor(target?)`             | Open a door or gate                                              |
199: | `openBank()`                    | Open nearest bank                                                |
200: | `depositItem(target, amount?)`  | Deposit item to bank                                             |
201: | `withdrawItem(slot, amount?)`   | Withdraw item from bank                                          |
202: | `closeInterface()`              | Close any open modal (shop, bank, book, quest scroll)            |
203: | `closeShop()` / `closeBank()`   | Close the shop / bank interface                                  |
204: | `openShop(target?)`             | Open shop via shopkeeper NPC                                     |
205: | `buyFromShop(target, amount?)`  | Buy item from open shop                                          |
206: | `sellToShop(target, amount?)`   | Sell item to open shop                                           |
207: | `equipItem(target)`             | Equip from inventory                                             |
208: | `unequipItem(target)`           | Unequip to inventory                                             |
209: | `eatFood(target)`               | Eat food, returns HP gained                                      |
210: | `useItemOnLoc(item, loc)`       | Use inventory item on loc (e.g. fish on range)                   |
211: | `useItemOnNpc(item, npc)`       | Use inventory item on NPC                                        |
212: | `burnLogs(target?)`             | Light logs with tinderbox                                        |
213: | `fletchLogs(product?)`          | Fletch logs with knife                                           |
214: | `craftLeather(product?)`        | Craft leather with needle                                        |
215: | `smithAtAnvil(product)`         | Smith bars at anvil                                              |
216: | `dismissBlockingUI()`           | Dismiss level-up dialogs (called automatically by all actions)   |
217: | `navigateDialog(choices)`       | Auto-click through dialog options                                |
218: | `skipTutorial()`                | Skip the tutorial island                                         |
219: 
220: ### sdk.\* Commonly Used Directly
221: 
222: | Method                                              | What it does                                        |
223: | --------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
224: | `getState()`                                        | Full world state snapshot                           |
225: | `getSkill(name)` / `getSkillXp(name)`               | Skill info                                          |
226: | `getInventory()` / `findInventoryItem(pattern)`     | Inventory queries                                   |
227: | `findNearbyNpc(pattern)` / `findNearbyLoc(pattern)` | Find nearby entities                                |
228: | `findNearbyPlayer(pattern)` / `getNearbyPlayers()`  | Find other players                                  |
229: | `findGroundItem(pattern)`                           | Find ground items                                   |
230: | `getDialog()`                                       | Current dialog state                                |
231: | `sendClickDialog(option)`                           | Click dialog option by its published `index`        |
232: | `clickDialogByText(pattern)`                        | Click dialog option by label — prefer this          |
233: | `sendClickComponent(id)`                            | Click interface button                              |
234: | `sendCloseModal()` / `sendCloseShop()`              | Close the open modal / shop                         |
235: | `sendDropItem(slot)`                                | Drop inventory item                                 |
236: | `sendUseItem(slot)`                                 | Use inventory item (bury, etc.)                     |
237: | `sendUseItemOnItem(src, dst)`                       | Combine two items                                   |
238: | `say(text)`                                         | Send chat, auto-chunked past the length cap         |
239: | `dm(name, text)`                                    | Send a private message, auto-chunked                |
240: | `getChat(opts?)` / `getNewChat(opts?)`              | Read chat history (500-deep) / only unseen messages |
241: | `waitForChat(opts?)`                                | Wait for a message (`{from, matching, timeout}`)    |
242: | `waitForCondition(pred)`                            | Wait for state predicate                            |
243: | `waitForTicks(n)`                                   | Wait n game ticks                                   |
244: | `scanNearbyLocs(radius?)`                           | Async extended-range loc scan; must be awaited      |
245: 
246: See `sdk/API.md` for exact async signatures, parameter defaults, and return
247: types.
248: 
249: ### Code environments
250: 
251: MCP `execute_code` exposes `bot` and `sdk` directly. Standalone
252: `bots/{username}/*.ts` files must import `runScript` and receive
253: `{ bot, sdk }` in its callback. Do not paste runner-context expressions into
254: `execute_code`.
255: 
256: Only one control connection should own a bot. Use observe mode for read-only
257: monitoring, avoid overlapping action programs on the same bot, and inspect
258: `sdk.getStateAge()` before acting after a disconnect or long pause.
259: 
260: ---
261: 
262: ### Modals Hide the Inventory
263: 
264: A shop or bank modal replaces the inventory tab, so the server rejects
265: inventory packets sent underneath it as "component not visible" — with no game
266: message. Close the modal before doing anything else:
267: 
268: ```typescript
269: await bot.closeInterface(); // any modal
270: await bot.closeShop(); // shop specifically
271: await sdk.sendCloseModal(); // low-level
272: ```
273: 
274: Don't click the interface's own "Close Window" component id. It's a
275: client-side close button with no server trigger; the SDK now routes those to a
276: close for you, but the named methods above are what to reach for.
277: 
278: ### Dialog Options Are Not In Product Order
279: 
280: Skill dialogs (fletching, crafting) publish four buttons _per product_ — Make
281: X, Make 10, Make 5, then one labelled with the product name. Arrow shafts are
282: option 4 of 12, not option 1. Never assume ordering:
283: 
284: ```typescript
285: const dialog = sdk.getDialog();
286: console.log(dialog?.options.map((o) => `${o.index}: ${o.text}`));
287: await sdk.clickDialogByText(/arrow shaft/i); // or bot.fletchLogs('arrow shaft')
288: ```
289: 
290: ### Dismiss Level-Up Dialogs
291: 
292: All BotActions methods automatically dismiss blocking UI (level-up dialogs, etc.) before executing. You don't need to call this manually in loops.
293: 
294: ```typescript
295: // Only needed if using low-level sdk methods directly:
296: await bot.dismissBlockingUI();
297: 
298: // Or manually check
299: if (sdk.getState()?.dialog.isOpen) {
300:   await sdk.sendClickDialog(0);
301: }
302: ```
303: 
304: ### Error Handling
305: 
306: ```typescript
307: const result = await bot.chopTree();
308: if (!result.success) {
309:   console.log(`Failed: ${result.message}`);
310:   // Handle failure - maybe walk somewhere else
311: }
312: ```
313: 
314: ## Project Structure
315: 
316: ```
317: 
318: bots/
319: └── {username}/
320:     ├── bot.env        # Credentials (BOT_USERNAME, PASSWORD, SERVER)
321:     ├── lab_log.md     # Session notes and observations
322:     └── script.ts      # Current script
323: 
324: sdk/
325: ├── index.ts           # BotSDK (low-level)
326: ├── actions.ts         # BotActions (high-level)
327: ├── cli.ts             # CLI for checking state
328: └── types.ts           # Type definitions
329: 
330: learnings/
331: ├── banking.md
332: └── ...etc
333: 
334: wiki/
335: ├── npcs/
336: ├── items/
337: ├── skills/
338: └── shops/
339: 
340: ```
341: 
342: ## Troubleshooting
343: 
344: **"No game client is attached" / "No state received"** - No client is publishing state for the bot. Start the lite client (`cd server/webclient && bun src/lite/runner.ts {username}`) or open the bot's browser URL, then rerun.
345: 
346: **"Client out of date" / "the server now runs revision N" / lite runner exits with code 3** - The game server was upgraded to a new game revision. Update your checkout (`git pull`, then `cd server/webclient && bun install`) and restart the lite runner. Browser clients only need a page reload.
347: 
348: **Script stalls** - Check for open dialogs (`state.dialog.isOpen`). Level-ups block everything.
349: 
350: **"Can't reach"** - Path is blocked. Try walking closer first, or find a different target.
351: 
352: **Wrong target** - Use more specific regex patterns: `/^tree$/i` not `/tree/i` (which matches "tree stump").
353: 
354: **Everything succeeds and nothing happens** - The two silent failure modes. A
355: `send*` returning success only means the client wrote bytes; it is not an ack.
356: 
357: - **The client never sent anything.** The client pathfinds before every interaction, and when it can't route it returns `cant_reach` without writing a packet - so the server never replies "I can't reach that!" either. Check `reachable` on the target before using it. `find*` already prefers reachable matches; pass `{reachable: true}` to get `null` instead of an unreachable one.
358: - **The server discarded the op.** A refused op (mid-action, stunned, target gone or out of view, bad option) gets `UNSET_MAP_FLAG` and nothing else - no message, no error. A blocking modal is worse: the op is accepted and the trigger never runs. Check `state.opFeedback.opRejectedCount` around a send, and gate loops on an observed effect rather than on a timer.
359: 
360: Start small and build up!

(End of file - total 360 lines)
</content>

# RS-Agent Bot Guide

You're here to play the mmo game through the progressive development of botting scripts, starting small then adapting to your desires and ideas.

## First Time Setup

**Create a new bot using the setup script:**

Ask the user for a bot name (max 12 chars, alphanumeric). If they skip, use the command without a username to auto-generate a random 9-character name.

```bash
# With custom username
bun bots/create-bot.ts {username}

# Auto-generate random username
bun bots/create-bot.ts

# Use local server (sets SERVER=localhost in bot.env)
bun bots/create-bot.ts {username} --local

# Use a custom server
bun bots/create-bot.ts {username} --server=myserver.example.com
```

This automatically creates:

- `bots/{username}/bot.env` - Credentials with auto-generated password
- `bots/{username}/lab_log.md` - Session notes template
- `bots/{username}/script.ts` - Ready-to-run starter script

### Start a Game Client (scripts only)

Scripts (`bun bots/{username}/*.ts`) and `bun sdk/cli.ts` need a running game
client; they never start one. Before running a script, start the headless lite
client in the background and leave it running:

```bash
cd server/webclient && bun install && bun src/lite/runner.ts {username}
```

It logs `Gateway connected, registering as '{username}'` once it's ready. One
process per bot; it exits non-zero if the game session ends. Without it, a
script exits with `No game client is attached`. MCP `execute_code` doesn't need
this step; it opens a browser client itself.

### Quick Start

1. Install dependencies: `bun install` (from project root)
2. Open project in your AI coding tool — the MCP server will be available automatically
3. Control your bot with suggestions.

### Tools

| Tool                           | Description                                    |
| ------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `execute_code(bot_name, code)` | Run code on a bot. Auto-connects on first use. |
| `list_bots()`                  | List connected bots                            |
| `disconnect_bot(name)`         | Disconnect a bot                               |

### Example

```typescript
// Just execute - auto-connects on first use
execute_code({
  bot_name: "mybot",
  code: `
    const state = sdk.getState();
    console.log('Position:', state.player.worldX, state.player.worldZ);

    // Chop trees for 1 minute
    const endTime = Date.now() + 60_000;
    while (Date.now() < endTime) {
      const tree = sdk.findNearbyLoc(/^tree$/i);
      if (tree) await bot.chopTree(tree);
    }

    return sdk.getInventory();
  `,
});
```

See `mcp/README.md` for detailed API reference.

Code runs in an async context with `bot` (BotActions) and `sdk` (BotSDK) available as globals.

## Reporting SDK Bugs

When the SDK has a bug or rough edge, first find a workaround, then file a report. One command, no auth, no permission needed:

```bash
bun sdk/bug-report.ts "incorrect results from bot.foo(), had to use raw sdk.sendFoo() instead for xyz reason."
```

Important note: The game itself is extremely well tested and complete, it's not buggy. If you can't figure out how to do something, don't blame the game, blame your assumptions and keep investigating. File a bug report _after_ you figure out
what's going on, don't just assume the game is broken because you got confused, and give up. The SDK is a thin layer on top of the game, and the game is the source of truth.

After filing the bug, keep working on your goal!

## Session Workflow

This is a **persistent character** - you don't restart fresh each time. The workflow is:

### 1. Check World State First

Before writing any script, check where the bot is and what it has:

```bash
bun sdk/cli.ts {username}
```

This shows: position, inventory, skills, nearby NPCs/objects, and more.

**Exception**: Skip this if you just created the character and know it's at spawn.

**Tutorial Check**: If the character is in the tutorial area, call `await bot.skipTutorial()` before running any other scripts. The tutorial blocks normal gameplay.

### 2. Write Your Script

Edit `bots/{username}/script_name.ts` with your goal. Keep scripts focused on one task. you may write multiple scripts for different tasks and switch between them.

### 3. Run the Script

```bash
bun bots/{username}/script_name.ts
```

### 4. Observe and Iterate

Watch the output. After the script finishes (or fails), check state again:

```bash
bun sdk/cli.ts {username}
```

Record observations in `lab_log.md`, then improve the script.

### Chatting Without Taking Control

To talk in-game (or read chat) without disturbing whatever script currently
owns the bot, use the chat CLI — it connects in `observe` mode, which can send
chat (and nothing else) and never pre-empts (or gets pre-empted by) a
controller:

```bash

bun sdk/chat.ts {username} --to {player} "on my way"  # send a private message
bun sdk/chat.ts {username}                          # recent chat
bun sdk/chat.ts {username} --watch                  # tail live
```

Public chat is capped at 400 chars per message; `sdk.say()` auto-splits longer
text into wire-safe chunks.

Private messages (`sdk.dm(name, text)` / `sdk.sendPrivateMessage(name, msg)`)
reach the target anywhere in the world - no friends-list setup needed - and
show up in `getChat()` as type 3 (received) / 6 (sent). The server accepts one
social packet (say or PM) per tick; `dm()` paces its chunks automatically.

## Script Duration Guidelines

**Start short, extend as you gain confidence:**

| Duration      | Use When                                              |
| ------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| **10s**       | New script, single actions, untested logic, debugging |
| **30s-1 min** | Validated approach, building confidence               |
| **5+ min**    | Proven strategy, grinding runs. USE SPARINGLY         |

A failed 5-minute run wastes more time than five 30 second diagnostic runs. **Fail fast and start simple.**

Look out for "I can't reach" messages - the solution is often to open closed gates or that the item isn't accessible.

| `interactLoc(target, option?)`  | Walk to loc, interact with any option (e.g. `'mine'`, `'smelt'`) |

| `castSpell(target, spell)`      | Cast a combat spell on an NPC or player                         |
| `pickpocketNpc(target)`         | Pickpocket NPC, detects XP gain vs stun                          |
| `chopTree(target?)`             | Chop tree, wait for logs                                         |
| `pickupItem(target)`            | Pick up ground item                                              |
| `openDoor(target?)`             | Open a door or gate                                              |
| `openBank()`                    | Open nearest bank                                                |
| `depositItem(target, amount?)`  | Deposit item to bank                                             |
| `withdrawItem(slot, amount?)`   | Withdraw item from bank                                          |
| `closeInterface()`              | Close any open modal (shop, bank, book, quest scroll)            |
| `closeShop()` / `closeBank()`   | Close the shop / bank interface                                  |
| `openShop(target?)`             | Open shop via shopkeeper NPC                                     |

| `sellToShop(target, amount?)`   | Sell item to open shop                                           |
| `equipItem(target)`             | Equip from inventory                                             |
| `unequipItem(target)`           | Unequip to inventory                                             |
| `eatFood(target)`               | Eat food, returns HP gained                                      |
| `useItemOnLoc(item, loc)`       | Use inventory item on loc (e.g. fish on range)                   |
| `useItemOnNpc(item, npc)`       | Use inventory item on NPC                                        |
| `burnLogs(target?)`             | Light logs with tinderbox                                        |
| `fletchLogs(product?)`          | Fletch logs with knife                                           |
| `craftLeather(product?)`        | Craft leather with needle                                        |
| `smithAtAnvil(product)`         | Smith bars at anvil                                              |
| `dismissBlockingUI()`           | Dismiss level-up dialogs (called automatically by all actions)   |
| `navigateDialog(choices)`       | Auto-click through dialog options                                |
| `skipTutorial()`                | Skip the tutorial island                                         |

### sdk.\* Commonly Used Directly

| Method                                              | What it does                                        |
| --------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `getState()`                                        | Full world state snapshot                           |
| `getSkill(name)` / `getSkillXp(name)`               | Skill info                                          |
| `getInventory()` / `findInventoryItem(pattern)`     | Inventory queries                                   |
| `findNearbyNpc(pattern)` / `findNearbyLoc(pattern)` | Find nearby entities                                |
| `findNearbyPlayer(pattern)` / `getNearbyPlayers()`  | Find other players                                  |
| `findGroundItem(pattern)`                           | Find ground items                                   |
| `getDialog()`                                       | Current dialog state                                |
| `sendClickDialog(option)`                           | Click dialog option by its published `index`        |
| `clickDialogByText(pattern)`                        | Click dialog option by label — prefer this          |
| `sendClickComponent(id)`                            | Click interface button                              |
| `sendCloseModal()` / `sendCloseShop()`              | Close the open modal / shop                         |
| `sendDropItem(slot)`                                | Drop inventory item                                 |
| `sendUseItem(slot)`                                 | Use inventory item (bury, etc.)                     |
| `sendUseItemOnItem(src, dst)`                       | Combine two items                                   |
| `say(text)`                                         | Send chat, auto-chunked past the length cap         |
| `dm(name, text)`                                    | Send a private message, auto-chunked                |
| `getChat(opts?)` / `getNewChat(opts?)`              | Read chat history (500-deep) / only unseen messages |
| `waitForChat(opts?)`                                | Wait for a message (`{from, matching, timeout}`)    |
| `waitForCondition(pred)`                            | Wait for state predicate                            |
| `waitForTicks(n)`                                   | Wait n game ticks                                   |
| `scanNearbyLocs(radius?)`                           | Async extended-range loc scan; must be awaited      |

See `sdk/API.md` for exact async signatures, parameter defaults, and return
types.

### Code environments

MCP `execute_code` exposes `bot` and `sdk` directly. Standalone
`bots/{username}/*.ts` files must import `runScript` and receive
`{ bot, sdk }` in its callback. Do not paste runner-context expressions into
`execute_code`.

Only one control connection should own a bot. Use observe mode for read-only
monitoring, avoid overlapping action programs on the same bot, and inspect
`sdk.getStateAge()` before acting after a disconnect or long pause.

---

### Modals Hide the Inventory

A shop or bank modal replaces the inventory tab, so the server rejects
inventory packets sent underneath it as "component not visible" — with no game
message. Close the modal before doing anything else:

```typescript
await bot.closeInterface(); // any modal
await bot.closeShop(); // shop specifically
await sdk.sendCloseModal(); // low-level
```

Don't click the interface's own "Close Window" component id. It's a
client-side close button with no server trigger; the SDK now routes those to a
close for you, but the named methods above are what to reach for.

### Dialog Options Are Not In Product Order

Skill dialogs (fletching, crafting) publish four buttons _per product_ — Make
X, Make 10, Make 5, then one labelled with the product name. Arrow shafts are
option 4 of 12, not option 1. Never assume ordering:

```typescript
const dialog = sdk.getDialog();
console.log(dialog?.options.map((o) => `${o.index}: ${o.text}`));
await sdk.clickDialogByText(/arrow shaft/i); // or bot.fletchLogs('arrow shaft')
```

### Dismiss Level-Up Dialogs

All BotActions methods automatically dismiss blocking UI (level-up dialogs, etc.) before executing. You don't need to call this manually in loops.

```typescript
// Only needed if using low-level sdk methods directly:
await bot.dismissBlockingUI();

// Or manually check
if (sdk.getState()?.dialog.isOpen) {
  await sdk.sendClickDialog(0);
}
```

### Error Handling

```typescript
const result = await bot.chopTree();
if (!result.success) {
  console.log(`Failed: ${result.message}`);
  // Handle failure - maybe walk somewhere else
}
```

## Project Structure

```

bots/
└── {username}/
    ├── bot.env        # Credentials (BOT_USERNAME, PASSWORD, SERVER)
    ├── lab_log.md     # Session notes and observations
    └── script.ts      # Current script

sdk/
├── index.ts           # BotSDK (low-level)
├── actions.ts         # BotActions (high-level)
├── cli.ts             # CLI for checking state
└── types.ts           # Type definitions

learnings/
├── banking.md
└── ...etc

wiki/
├── npcs/
├── items/
├── skills/
└── shops/

```

## Troubleshooting

**"No game client is attached" / "No state received"** - No client is publishing state for the bot. Start the lite client (`cd server/webclient && bun src/lite/runner.ts {username}`) or open the bot's browser URL, then rerun.

**"Client out of date" / "the server now runs revision N" / lite runner exits with code 3** - The game server was upgraded to a new game revision. Update your checkout (`git pull`, then `cd server/webclient && bun install`) and restart the lite runner. Browser clients only need a page reload.

**Script stalls** - Check for open dialogs (`state.dialog.isOpen`). Level-ups block everything.

**"Can't reach"** - Path is blocked. Try walking closer first, or find a different target.

**Wrong target** - Use more specific regex patterns: `/^tree$/i` not `/tree/i` (which matches "tree stump").

**Everything succeeds and nothing happens** - The two silent failure modes. A
`send*` returning success only means the client wrote bytes; it is not an ack.

- **The client never sent anything.** The client pathfinds before every interaction, and when it can't route it returns `cant_reach` without writing a packet - so the server never replies "I can't reach that!" either. Check `reachable` on the target before using it. `find*` already prefers reachable matches; pass `{reachable: true}` to get `null` instead of an unreachable one.
- **The server discarded the op.** A refused op (mid-action, stunned, target gone or out of view, bad option) gets `UNSET_MAP_FLAG` and nothing else - no message, no error. A blocking modal is worse: the op is accepted and the trigger never runs. Check `state.opFeedback.opRejectedCount` around a send, and gate loops on an observed effect rather than on a timer.

Start small and build up!

181: function parseIniConfigs(content: string, sourcePath: string): Map<string, NpcConfig> {
182:     const configs = new Map<string, NpcConfig>();
183:     let current: NpcConfig | null = null;
184: 
185:     for (const rawLine of content.split('\n')) {
186:         const line = rawLine.trim();
187:         // skip comments
188:         if (line.startsWith('//') || line.startsWith('/ ')) continue;
189: 
190:         const sectionMatch = line.match(/^\[([^\]]+)\]$/);
191:         if (sectionMatch) {
192:             if (current) configs.set(current.configName, current);
193:             current = makeEmptyConfig(sectionMatch[1], sourcePath);
194:             continue;
195:         }
196: 
197:         if (!current || !line || line === '') {
198:             continue;
199:         }
200: 
201:         const eqIdx = line.indexOf('=');
202:         if (eqIdx === -1) continue;
203:         const key = line.slice(0, eqIdx).trim();
204:         const value = line.slice(eqIdx + 1).trim();
205: 
206:         switch (key) {
207:             case 'name': current.name = value; break;
208:             case 'desc': current.desc = value; break;
209:             case 'vislevel': current.vislevel = value; break;
210:             case 'hitpoints': current.hitpoints = parseInt(value) || 0; break;
211:             case 'attack': current.attack = parseInt(value) || 0; break;
212:             case 'strength': current.strength = parseInt(value) || 0; break;
213:             case 'defence': current.defence = parseInt(value) || 0; break;
214:             case 'category': current.category = value; break;
215:             case 'huntmode': current.huntmode = value; break;
216:             case 'wanderrange': current.wanderrange = parseInt(value) || 0; break;
217:             case 'maxrange': current.maxrange = parseInt(value) || 0; break;
218:             case 'respawnrate': current.respawnrate = parseInt(value) || 0; break;
219:             case 'defaultmode': current.defaultmode = value; break;
220:             case 'givechase': current.givechase = value; break;
221:             case 'moverestrict': current.moverestrict = value; break;
222:             case 'op1': current.ops[0] = value; break;
223:             case 'op2': current.ops[1] = value; break;
224:             case 'op3': current.ops[2] = value; break;
225:             case 'op4': current.ops[3] = value; break;
226:             case 'op5': current.ops[4] = value; break;
227:             case 'param': {
228:                 const commaIdx = value.indexOf(',');
229:                 if (commaIdx !== -1) {
230:                     current.params.set(value.slice(0, commaIdx), value.slice(commaIdx + 1));
231:                 }
232:                 break;
233:             }
234:             default: {
235:                 if (key.startsWith('patrol')) {
236:                     current.hasPatrol = true;
237:                 }
238:                 break;
239:             }
240:         }
241:     }
242:     if (current) configs.set(current.configName, current);
243:     return configs;
244: }

311:         const name = line.slice(eqIdx + 1).trim();
312:         if (!isNaN(id) && name) {

322: function parseMapSpawns(
323:     mapsDir: string,
324:     npcIdToName: Map<number, string>
325: ): Map<string, SpawnLocation[]> {
326:     const spawns = new Map<string, SpawnLocation[]>();
327:     const mapFiles = readdirSync(mapsDir).filter(f => f.endsWith('.jm2'));
328: 
329:     for (const file of mapFiles) {
330:         const match = file.match(/^m(\d+)_(\d+)\.jm2$/);
331:         if (!match) continue;
332:         const mapX = parseInt(match[1]);
333:         const mapZ = parseInt(match[2]);
334:         const mapSquare = `m${mapX}_${mapZ}`;
335: 
336:         const content = readFileSync(join(mapsDir, file), 'utf-8');
337:         const npcSectionStart = content.indexOf('==== NPC ====');
338:         if (npcSectionStart === -1) continue;
339: 
340:         const afterNpc = content.slice(npcSectionStart + '==== NPC ===='.length);
341:         // NPC section goes until the next ==== or end of file
342:         const nextSection = afterNpc.indexOf('====');
343:         const npcBlock = nextSection === -1 ? afterNpc : afterNpc.slice(0, nextSection);
344: 
345:         for (const line of npcBlock.split('\n')) {
346:             const trimmed = line.trim();
347:             if (!trimmed) continue;
348:             // Format: level localX localZ: npcID
349:             const m = trimmed.match(/^(\d+)\s+(\d+)\s+(\d+):\s*(\d+)$/);
350:             if (!m) continue;
351:             const level = parseInt(m[1]);
352:             const localX = parseInt(m[2]);
353:             const localZ = parseInt(m[3]);
354:             const npcId = parseInt(m[4]);
355: 
356:             const configName = npcIdToName.get(npcId);
357:             if (!configName) continue;
358: 
359:             const globalX = mapX * 64 + localX;
360:             const globalZ = mapZ * 64 + localZ;
361: 
362:             if (!spawns.has(configName)) spawns.set(configName, []);
363:             spawns.get(configName)!.push({ mapX, mapZ, globalX, globalZ, level, mapSquare });
364:         }
365:     }
366: 
367:     return spawns;
368: }

372: interface ParsedDropFile {
373:     triggers: Map<string, string>; // configName/category -> label name (or "inline")
374:     labels: Map<string, DropTableData>; // label name -> parsed data
375: }
376: 
377: interface DropTableData {
378:     hasDeathDrop: boolean;
379:     entries: DropEntry[];
380:     alwaysItems: AlwaysDrop[];
381:     clueTier: string | null;
382: }
383: 
384: function parseDropTables(dropsDir: string): Map<string, DropTable> {
385:     const files = readdirSync(dropsDir).filter(f => f.endsWith('.rs2') && f !== 'shared_droptables.rs2' && f !== 'drop_table.rs2');
386: 
387:     // Map from trigger name (config name or _category) to DropTable
388:     const result = new Map<string, DropTable>();
389: 
390:     for (const file of files) {
391:         const content = readFileSync(join(dropsDir, file), 'utf-8');
392:         const parsed = parseDropFile(content);
393: 
394:         for (const [triggerName, target] of parsed.triggers) {
395:             const data = parsed.labels.get(target);
396:             if (!data) continue;
397: 
398:             if (!result.has(target)) {
399:                 result.set(target, {
400:                     triggerNames: [],
401:                     alwaysDrop: data.hasDeathDrop,
402:                     entries: data.entries,
403:                     alwaysDropItems: data.alwaysItems,
404:                     clueTier: data.clueTier,
405:                 });
406:             }
407:             result.get(target)!.triggerNames.push(triggerName);
408:         }
409:     }
410: 
411:     return result;
412: }
413: 
414: function parseDropFile(content: string): ParsedDropFile {
415:     const triggers = new Map<string, string>();
416:     const labels = new Map<string, DropTableData>();
417: 
418:     const lines = content.split('\n');
419:     let currentLabel: string | null = null;
420:     let currentData: DropTableData | null = null;
421:     let denominator = 128; // default
422:     let lastThreshold = 0;
423: 
424:     function finishLabel() {
425:         if (currentLabel && currentData) {
426:             labels.set(currentLabel, currentData);
427:         }
428:     }
429: 
430:     for (let i = 0; i < lines.length; i++) {
431:         const line = lines[i].trim();
432:         if (!line || line.startsWith('//')) continue;
433: 
434:         // Trigger line: [ai_queue3,name] @label; or [ai_queue3,name] without @
435:         const triggerMatch = line.match(/^\[ai_queue3,([^\]]+)\]\s*(?:@(\w+)\s*;)?/);
436:         if (triggerMatch) {
437:             const triggerName = triggerMatch[1];
438:             const labelRef = triggerMatch[2];
439: 
440:             if (labelRef) {
441:                 triggers.set(triggerName, labelRef);
442:             } else {
443:                 // Inline drop table - use trigger name as label
444:                 finishLabel();
445:                 currentLabel = `_inline_${triggerName}`;
446:                 currentData = { hasDeathDrop: false, entries: [], alwaysItems: [], clueTier: null };
447:                 denominator = 128;
448:                 lastThreshold = 0;
449:                 triggers.set(triggerName, currentLabel);
450:             }
451:             continue;
452:         }
453: 
454:         // Label line: [label,name]
455:         const labelMatch = line.match(/^\[label,(\w+)\]/);
456:         if (labelMatch) {
457:             finishLabel();
458:             currentLabel = labelMatch[1];
459:             currentData = { hasDeathDrop: false, entries: [], alwaysItems: [], clueTier: null };
460:             denominator = 128;
461:             lastThreshold = 0;
462:             continue;
463:         }
464: 
465:         if (!currentData) continue;
466: 
467:         // Death drop line
468:         if (line.includes('npc_param(death_drop)')) {
469:             currentData.hasDeathDrop = true;
470:             continue;
471:         }
472: 
473:         // Clue scroll detection
474:         if (line.includes('trail_easycluedrop')) {
475:             currentData.clueTier = 'easy';
476:         } else if (line.includes('trail_mediumcluedrop')) {
477:             currentData.clueTier = currentData.clueTier === 'easy' ? 'easy' : 'medium';
478:         } else if (line.includes('trail_hardcluedrop')) {
479:             currentData.clueTier = currentData.clueTier ? currentData.clueTier : 'hard';
480:         }
481: 
482:         // Random declaration: def_int $random = random(N);
483:         const randomMatch = line.match(/random\((\d+)\)/);
484:         if (randomMatch && line.includes('def_int')) {
485:             denominator = parseInt(randomMatch[1]);
486:             lastThreshold = 0;
487:             continue;
488:         }
489: 
490:         // Always-drop items (outside the if/else chain, plain obj_add)
491:         // These come after the death_drop line but before the random() declaration
492:         if (line.includes('obj_add(npc_coord,') && !line.includes('npc_param(death_drop)') && !currentData.entries.length) {
493:             const alwaysMatch = line.match(/obj_add\(npc_coord,\s*([^,]+),\s*(\d+)/);
494:             if (alwaysMatch && !line.includes('$random') && !line.includes('$drop') && !line.includes('$rng')) {
495:                 // Check if we're inside an if block - simple heuristic: no if/else context
496:                 const prevLines = lines.slice(Math.max(0, i - 3), i).join(' ');
497:                 if (!prevLines.includes('if (') && !prevLines.includes('else if') && !prevLines.includes('random(')) {
498:                     currentData.alwaysItems.push({
499:                         itemConfigName: alwaysMatch[1].trim(),
500:                         quantity: parseInt(alwaysMatch[2]),
501:                     });
502:                     continue;
503:                 }
504:             }
505:         }
506: 
507:         // If/else if threshold: if ($random < N) or else if ($random < N) or ($dropint < N) or ($rng < N)
508:         const threshMatch = line.match(/(?:if|else\s+if)\s*\(\s*\$\w+\s*<\s*(\d+)\s*\)/);
509:         if (threshMatch) {
510:             const newThreshold = parseInt(threshMatch[1]);
511:             const numerator = newThreshold - lastThreshold;
512: 
513:             // Collect all lines belonging to this branch until the next } else if or closing }
514:             const blockLines: string[] = [line];
515:             for (let j = i + 1; j < Math.min(i + 15, lines.length); j++) {
516:                 const jline = lines[j].trim();
517:                 // Stop at next else-if branch or end of chain
518:                 if (jline.startsWith('} else if') || jline === '}') break;
519:                 blockLines.push(jline);
520:             }
521:             const block = blockLines.join('\n');
522: 
523:             // Check for members-only variant
524:             const membersCheck = block.includes('map_members = ^true');
525:             const hasFallback = block.includes('} else {');
526: 
527:             // Parse obj_add calls with awareness of members/F2P branches
528:             // obj_add patterns: obj_add(npc_coord, item, qty, duration) or obj_add(npc_coord, ~func, duration)
529:             const objAddPattern = /obj_add\(npc_coord,\s*([^,)]+),\s*(.+?),\s*\^lootdrop_duration\)/g;
530:             const sharedCallPattern = /obj_add\(npc_coord,\s*~(\w+),\s*\^lootdrop_duration\)/g;
531: 
532:             if (membersCheck && hasFallback) {
533:                 // Split block into members and F2P sections
534:                 const membersIdx = block.indexOf('map_members = ^true');
535:                 const elseIdx = block.indexOf('} else {', membersIdx);
536:                 const membersBlock = block.slice(membersIdx, elseIdx || block.length);
537:                 const f2pBlock = elseIdx !== -1 ? block.slice(elseIdx) : '';
538: 
539:                 // Add members items
540:                 for (const m of membersBlock.matchAll(objAddPattern)) {
541:                     const itemName = m[1].trim();
542:                     const rawQty = m[2].trim();
543:                     if (itemName.startsWith('~')) continue;
544:                     currentData.entries.push({
545:                         itemConfigName: itemName,
546:                         quantity: parseQuantity(rawQty),
547:                         numerator, denominator,
548:                         membersOnly: true,
549:                     });
550:                 }
551:                 for (const m of membersBlock.matchAll(sharedCallPattern)) {
552:                     currentData.entries.push({
553:                         itemConfigName: `~${m[1]}`, quantity: '1',
554:                         numerator, denominator, membersOnly: true,
555:                     });
556:                 }
557: 
558:                 // Add F2P fallback items
559:                 for (const m of f2pBlock.matchAll(objAddPattern)) {
560:                     const itemName = m[1].trim();
561:                     const rawQty = m[2].trim();
562:                     if (itemName.startsWith('~')) continue;
563:                     currentData.entries.push({
564:                         itemConfigName: itemName,
565:                         quantity: parseQuantity(rawQty),
566:                         numerator, denominator,
567:                         membersOnly: false,
568:                     });
569:                 }
570:             } else {
571:                 // Regular block (no members split, or members-only with no fallback)
572:                 const isMembers = membersCheck && !hasFallback;
573: 
574:                 for (const m of block.matchAll(objAddPattern)) {
575:                     const itemName = m[1].trim();
576:                     const rawQty = m[2].trim();
577:                     if (itemName.startsWith('~')) continue;
578:                     currentData.entries.push({
579:                         itemConfigName: itemName,
580:                         quantity: parseQuantity(rawQty),
581:                         numerator, denominator,
582:                         membersOnly: isMembers,
583:                     });
584:                 }
585:                 for (const m of block.matchAll(sharedCallPattern)) {
586:                     currentData.entries.push({
587:                         itemConfigName: `~${m[1]}`, quantity: '1',
588:                         numerator, denominator, membersOnly: isMembers,
589:                     });
590:                 }
591:             }
592: 
593:             lastThreshold = newThreshold;
594:             continue;
595:         }
596:     }
597: 
598:     finishLabel();
599:     return { triggers, labels };
600: }

602: // ─── Parse Quantity Expression ────────────────────────────────────────────────
603: 
604: function parseQuantity(raw: string): string {
605:     const rangeMatch = raw.match(/~random_range\((\d+)\s*,\s*(\d+)\)/);
606:     if (rangeMatch) return `${rangeMatch[1]}-${rangeMatch[2]}`;
607:     // Plain integer
608:     const num = parseInt(raw);
609:     if (!isNaN(num)) return String(num);
610:     return raw;
611: }

615: function prettifyConfigName(name: string): string {
616:     return name
617:         .replace(/_/g, ' ')
618:         .replace(/\b(\d+)\b/g, '$1') // keep numbers
619:         .replace(/\b\w/g, c => c.toUpperCase())
620:         .replace(/\bcert\b/i, 'Certificate')
621:         .trim();
622: }

624: function getObjDisplayName(configName: string, objNames: Map<string, string>): string {
625:     // Handle shared table references
626:     if (configName === '~randomherb') return 'Herbs (varies)';
627:     if (configName === '~randomjewel') return 'Gems (varies)';
628:     if (configName === '~ultrarare_getitem') return 'Rare drop table';
629:     if (configName === '~megararetable') return 'Mega-rare drop table';
630:     if (configName === '~randomjunk') return 'Junk items (varies)';
631:     if (configName.startsWith('~')) return prettifyConfigName(configName.slice(1));
632: 
633:     return objNames.get(configName) || prettifyConfigName(configName);

652: function getMovementDesc(config: NpcConfig): string {

654:     if (config.moverestrict === 'nomove') return 'Stationary';

665:     if (dt.includes('slash')) return 'Slash';
666:     if (dt.includes('crush')) return 'Crush';
667:     if (dt.includes('magic')) return 'Magic';
668:     if (dt.includes('range')) return 'Ranged';
669:     return 'Crush'; // default

674: function isCombatNpc(config: NpcConfig): boolean {

682:         config.params.has('stabdefence') || config.params.has('slashdefence') ||
683:         config.params.has('crushdefence') || config.params.has('magicdefence') ||
684:         config.params.has('rangedefence');

972: // ─── Generate Markdown for One NPC Page ──────────────────────────────────────

974: function generateNpcMarkdown(page: NpcPage, objNames: Map<string, string>): string {
975:     const primary = page.variants[0];
976:     const combat = isCombatNpc(primary);
977:     const lines: string[] = [];
978: 
979:     // Title
980:     lines.push(`# ${page.displayName}`);
981:     lines.push('');
982: 
983:     // Info table
984:     lines.push('| Detail | |');
985:     lines.push('|---|---|');
986: 
987:     // Combat level - show range if variants differ
988:     const vislevels = [...new Set(page.variants.map(v => v.vislevel).filter(v => v && v !== 'hide'))];
989:     if (vislevels.length > 1) {
990:         const nums = vislevels.map(v => parseInt(v)).filter(n => !isNaN(n)).sort((a, b) => a - b);
991:         if (nums.length > 1) {
992:             lines.push(`| **Combat Level** | ${nums[0]}-${nums[nums.length - 1]} |`);
993:         } else {
994:             lines.push(`| **Combat Level** | ${vislevels[0]} |`);
995:         }
996:     } else if (vislevels.length === 1) {
997:         lines.push(`| **Combat Level** | ${vislevels[0]} |`);
998:     } else {
999:         lines.push('| **Combat Level** | None |');
1000:     }
1001: 
1002:     // Hitpoints
1003:     const hps = [...new Set(page.variants.map(v => v.hitpoints).filter(h => h > 0))].sort((a, b) => a - b);
1004:     if (hps.length > 1) {
1005:         lines.push(`| **Hitpoints** | ${hps[0]}-${hps[hps.length - 1]} |`);
1006:     } else if (hps.length === 1) {
1007:         lines.push(`| **Hitpoints** | ${hps[0]} |`);
1008:     } else {
1009:         lines.push('| **Hitpoints** | N/A |');
1010:     }
1011: 
1012:     // Description
1013:     lines.push(`| **Description** | ${primary.desc || 'N/A'} |`);

1: # SDK API Reference
2: 
3: > Auto-generated from TypeScript source. Do not edit directly.
4: > Run `bun run docs:api` to regenerate or `bun run docs:api:check` to verify it.
5: 
6: ## Execution model
7: 
8: - `bot.*` methods are high-level helpers. They attempt to observe method-specific evidence such as movement, inventory, XP, dialog, or state changes. When a method returns a result, inspect its `success` and any `reason` or `message`: the strength of completion evidence varies by method.
9: - `sdk.send*` methods are low-level browser-client dispatches. A successful `ActionResult` means the enhanced browser client accepted and dispatched the command; it does **not** prove that the game server processed it or that the intended game effect occurred.
10: - Methods whose signature returns `Promise<...>` are asynchronous and must be awaited. In particular, `scanNearbyLocs()` and `scanGroundItems()` return promises.
11: - `getInventory().length` is the number of occupied slots. `InventoryItem.count` is the quantity in that one slot, and `findInventoryItem()` returns the first matching slot rather than an aggregate across matching slots.
12: 
13: ## BotActions (high-level)
14: 
15: ### Grand Exchange
16: 
17: | Signature | Description |
18: |---|---|
19: | `async openGE(timeout: number = 15_000): Promise<GEActionResult>` | Walk to the physical exchange and open it. Requires updated client/server GE state support. |
20: | `async searchGE(query: string, side: 'buy' \| 'sell' = 'buy', timeout: number = 15_000): Promise<GEActionResult>` | Search the in-game catalogue in a free slot; returns acknowledged results in state.search. |
21: | `async placeGEOffer(request: GEOfferRequest, timeout: number = 30_000): Promise<GEActionResult>` | Place an inventory-funded offer at an already open exchange and verify the server receipt. Never retries confirmation. |
22: | `async cancelGEOffer(offerId: number, timeout: number = 15_000): Promise<GEActionResult>` | Cancel your offer's unfilled remainder; returned assets remain in collection. Uses offer ID, not slot. |
23: | `async collectGEOffer(offerId: number, notes: boolean = true, timeout: number = 15_000): Promise<GEActionResult>` | Collect one offer, optionally as notes. Reports actual backpack additions; overflow stays in collection. |
24: | `async collectGE(timeout: number = 15_000): Promise<GEActionResult>` | Collect every available claim as notes and coins; requires an open physical exchange. |
25: 
26: ### UI & Dialog
27: 
28: | Signature | Description |
29: |---|---|
30: | `async skipTutorial(options: { randomizeAppearance?: boolean } = {}): Promise<ActionResult>` | Skip tutorial by navigating dialogs and talking to tutorial NPCs. This is a porcelain method - domain logic that was moved from bot client. |
31: | `async dismissBlockingUI(): Promise<void>` | Dismiss any blocking UI like level-up dialogs. |
32: | `async waitForDialogClose(timeout: number = 30000): Promise<void>` | Wait for dialog to close. |
33: | `async navigateDialog(choices: (number \| string \| RegExp)[]): Promise<void>` | _No description provided._ |
34: 
35: ### Doors
36: 
37: | Signature | Description |
38: |---|---|
39: | `async openDoor(target?: NearbyLoc \| string \| RegExp): Promise<OpenDoorResult>` | Open a door or gate, walking to it if needed. |
40: 
41: ### Other
42: 
43: | Signature | Description |
44: |---|---|
45: | `async useItemOnLoc(item: InventoryItem \| string \| RegExp, loc: NearbyLoc \| string \| RegExp, options: { timeout?: number } = {}): Promise<UseItemOnLocResult>` | Use an inventory item on a nearby location (e.g., fish on range, ore on furnace). Walks to the location first (handling doors), then uses the item. |
46: | `async useItemOnNpc(item: InventoryItem \| string \| RegExp, npc: NearbyNpc \| string \| RegExp, options: { timeout?: number } = {}): Promise<UseItemOnNpcResult>` | Use an inventory item on a nearby NPC (e.g., bones on altar keeper, item on NPC). Walks to the NPC first (handling doors), then uses the item. |
47: | `async dropItem(target: InventoryItem \| string \| RegExp, amount: number \| 'all' = 'all'): Promise<DropItemResult>` | Drop inventory items by name, waiting for each drop to land before sending the next. `sendDropItem` on a slot the server has already emptied silently no-ops, so slot loops built on stale state lose most of their sends; this re-resolves the slot from fresh state every time. `amount` counts inventory slots (a whole stack drops as one). Pass `'all'` or `-1` to drop every matching slot. |
48: | `async closeInterface(timeout: number = 5000): Promise<ActionResult>` | Close any open modal interface (bank, book, quest scroll, etc.). |
49: 
50: ### Woodcutting & Firemaking
51: 
52: | Signature | Description |
53: |---|---|
54: | `async chopTree(target?: NearbyLoc \| string \| RegExp): Promise<ChopTreeResult>` | Chop a tree and wait for logs to appear in inventory. |
55: | `async burnLogs(logsTarget?: InventoryItem \| string \| RegExp): Promise<BurnLogsResult>` | Burn logs using a tinderbox, wait for firemaking XP. |
56: 
57: ### Items & Inventory
58: 
59: | Signature | Description |
60: |---|---|
61: | `async pickupItem(target: GroundItem \| string \| RegExp): Promise<PickupResult>` | Pick up an item from the ground. |
62: 
63: ### NPC & Object Interaction
64: 
65: | Signature | Description |

Any offer change resets both accepts server-side, so the offer seen at accept time is the offer that reaches the confirm screen; the confirm re-verification makes offer-switching structurally impossible to slip past this method. `options.requestTimeout` (default 30 s) bounds the trade request; `options.timeout` (default 60 s) bounds the open offer+confirm screens. Every close is classified as completed or declined, so `success: false` means nothing changed hands. |
| `async serveTrades(options: ServeTradesOptions = {}): Promise<ServeTradesResult>` | Serve incoming trades: wait for "wishes to trade with you." requests, accept ones matching the `from` filter, and run each session with the shared give/want/accept policy. The receiving half of a muling setup: ```ts // Worker: bot.trade('mule01', { give: [{ item: /ore/i, amount: -1 }] }) // Mule: bot.serveTrades({ from: /^fleet_/i, until: () => sdk.getInventory().length >= 26 }) ``` This owns the bot while running - it is an explicit serving loop, not a background hook, so it never fights another controller for the session. |

### Combat & Equipment

| Signature | Description |
|---|---|
| `async equipItem(target: InventoryItem \| string \| RegExp): Promise<EquipResult>` | Equip an item from inventory. |
| `async unequipItem(target: InventoryItem \| string \| RegExp): Promise<UnequipResult>` | Unequip an item to inventory. |
| `getEquipment(): InventoryItem[]` | Get all currently equipped items. |
| `findEquippedItem(pattern: string \| RegExp): InventoryItem \| null` | Find an equipped item by name pattern. |
| `async eatFood(target?: InventoryItem \| string \| RegExp): Promise<EatResult>` | Eat food to restore hitpoints. With no target, eats the first inventory item that offers Eat. |
| `async attack(target: CombatTarget, timeout: number = 5000): Promise<AttackResult>` | Attack an NPC or another player, walking to the target if needed. Takes either an entity (from `sdk.findNearbyNpc`/`sdk.findNearbyPlayer`) or a name/pattern, matched against NPCs first and players second - so pass the entity when a player shares a name with a monster. ```ts await bot.attack(/^chicken$/i); await bot.attack(sdk.findNearbyPlayer('Zezima')!); ``` PvP attacks are refused outside the wilderness and across too big a level gap; those come back as `reason: 'not_attackable'` with the server's own wording in `message`. |
| `async attackPlayer(target: NearbyPlayer \| string \| RegExp, timeout: number = 5000): Promise<AttackResult>` | Attack another player (OPPLAYER2). Prefer {@link attack}, which also takes NPCs. |
| `async castSpell(target: CombatTarget, spellComponent: number \| string, timeout: number = 3000): Promise<CastSpellResult>` | Cast a combat spell on an NPC or another player. The two are the same action to the server (OPNPCT vs OPPLAYERT), so this takes either: an entity from `sdk.findNearbyNpc`/`sdk.findNearbyPlayer`, or a name/pattern matched against NPCs first and players second. ```ts await bot.castSpell('goblin', Spells.WIND_STRIKE); await bot.castSpell(sdk.findNearbyPlayer('Zezima')!, Spells.FIRE_STRIKE); ``` Magic XP is the evidence of a cast landing, so a splash still counts as success with `hit: false`. |
| `async castSpellOnPlayer(target: NearbyPlayer \| string \| RegExp, spellComponent: number \| string, timeout: number = 3000): Promise<CastSpellResult>` | Cast a combat spell on another player (OPPLAYERT). Prefer {@link castSpell}. |

### Condition Waiting

| Signature | Description |
|---|---|
| `async waitForSkillLevel(skillName: string, targetLevel: number, timeout: number = 60000): Promise<SkillState>` | Wait until a skill reaches a target level. |
| `async waitForInventoryItem(pattern: string \| RegExp, timeout: number = 30000): Promise<InventoryItem>` | Wait until an item appears in inventory. |
| `async waitForIdle(timeout: number = 10000): Promise<void>` | Wait for player to stop moving. |

### Crafting & Smithing

| Signature | Description |
|---|---|
| `async fletchLogs(product?: string): Promise<FletchResult>` | Fletch logs into bows or arrow shafts using a knife. `product` is matched against the dialog's visible product labels ("15 Arrow Shafts", "Oak Short Bow", ...), so 'arrow shaft', 'shortbow' and 'oak long' all resolve. Omit it to take the first product offered. One call makes one batch — 15 shafts, or one bow. |
| `async craftLeather(product?: string): Promise<CraftLeatherResult>` | Craft leather into armour using needle and thread. |
| `async smithAtAnvil(product: string \| number = 'dagger', options: { barPattern?: RegExp; timeout?: number } = {}): Promise<SmithResult>` | Smith a bar into an item at an anvil. |
| `async craftJewelry(options: { barPattern?: RegExp; product?: string; gem?: string; timeout?: number; } = {}): Promise<CraftJewelryResult>` | Craft jewelry at a furnace using a gold/silver bar and optional gem. Requires: bar + mould in inventory (ring mould, necklace mould, or amulet mould). Optionally a gem for gem-set jewelry. |
| `async enchantItem(target: InventoryItem \| string \| RegExp, level: 1 \| 2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 5, options: { timeout?: number } = {}): Promise<EnchantResult>` | Cast an enchantment spell on a jewelry item. |
| `async stringAmulet(target: InventoryItem \| string \| RegExp = /amulet/i, options: { timeout?: number } = {}): Promise<StringAmuletResult>` | String an amulet using a ball of wool. |

### Mining

| Signature | Description |
|---|---|
| `async mineRock(target: NearbyLoc \| string \| RegExp = /rocks?/i, options: { timeout?: number } = {}): Promise<MineRockResult>` | Mine a rock and wait for new ore plus Mining XP. Rock names have a "Rocks" prefix: use /copper ore/i for rocks and /^copper ore$/i for inventory. |

### Prayer

| Signature | Description |
|---|---|
| `async activatePrayer(prayer: PrayerName \| number): Promise<PrayerResult>` | Activate a prayer by name or index. Checks preconditions (level, prayer points, not already active) before toggling. |
| `async deactivatePrayer(prayer: PrayerName \| number): Promise<PrayerResult>` | Deactivate a prayer by name or index. Checks if the prayer is actually active before toggling. |
| `async deactivateAllPrayers(): Promise<PrayerResult>` | Deactivate all currently active prayers. Toggles each active prayer off one by one. |

---

## BotSDK (low-level)

### Connection & Subscriptions

| Signature | Description |
|---|---|
| `async connect(): Promise<void>` | Connect to the gateway WebSocket. |
| `async disconnect(): Promise<void>` | Disconnect from the gateway. |
| `onConnectionStateChange(listener: (state: ConnectionState, attempt?: number) => void): () => void` | _No description provided._ |
| `onStateUpdate(listener: (state: BotWorldState) => void): () => void` | _No description provided._ |

### State Access

| Signature | Description |
|---|---|
| `isConnected(): boolean` | Check if WebSocket is connected. |
| `isAuthenticated(): boolean` | Check if the gateway has accepted our credentials. True means the transport and auth are both fine - if state is still missing after this, the problem is that no game client is logged in, not the connection. |
| `getConnectionState(): ConnectionState` | Get current connection state (connecting, connected, reconnecting, disconnected). |
| `getReconnectAttempt(): number` | Get current reconnection attempt number. |
| `getConnectionMode(): SDKConnectionMode` | Get connection mode (control or observe). |
| `async isBotConnected(): Promise<boolean>` | Check if bot is currently connected to gateway. |
| `getState(): BotWorldState \| null` | Get current game state snapshot. |
| `getStateReceivedAt(): number` | Get timestamp when state was last received (ms since epoch) |
| `getStateAge(): number` | Get age of current state in milliseconds |
| `getChat(opts: { limit?: number; types?: readonly number[]; includeSelf?: boolean } = {}): GameMessage[]` | Read recent chat messages. Returns player chat (public + PMs) by default, newest last. Reads from the SDK's accumulated history — up to 500 messages retained since connect — so old lines survive both system spam (level-ups, combat) and the client's own 100-deep ring eviction. |
| `getNewChat(opts: { types?: readonly number[]; includeSelf?: boolean } = {}): GameMessage[]` | Read only chat messages that have arrived since the last call (cursor-based, newest last). Repeat polls never re-show the same message — no need to hand-roll a baseline. The first call returns everything seen since connect. Excludes your own messages by default. |
| `getChatFrom(name: string, opts: { limit?: number } = {}): GameMessage[]` | Read recent chat from a specific sender (case-insensitive, substring match on name), newest last, from the accumulated history. Handy for "what did my partner say?" without regex-matching the sender field yourself. |
| `getSkill(name: string): SkillState \| null` | Get a skill by name (case-insensitive; "hp"/"hitpoint" alias Hitpoints). |
| `getSkillXp(name: string): number \| null` | Get XP for a skill by name. |
| `getSkills(): SkillState[]` | Get all skills. |
| `getInventoryItem(slot: number): InventoryItem \| null` | Get inventory item by slot number. |
| `findInventoryItem(pattern: string \| RegExp): InventoryItem \| null` | Find inventory item by name pattern (shortest matching name wins). |
| `getInventory(): InventoryItem[]` | Get all inventory items. The array is COMPACTED (empty slots are omitted), so its index is not the inventory slot. `sendUseItem` / `sendUseItemOnItem` / `sendDropItem` take slot numbers: always pass `item.slot`, never the array index. |
| `getEquipmentItem(slot: number): InventoryItem \| null` | Get equipment item by slot number. |
| `findEquipmentItem(pattern: string \| RegExp): InventoryItem \| null` | Find equipment item by name pattern (shortest matching name wins). |
| `getEquipment(): InventoryItem[]` | Get all equipped items. |
| `getBankItem(slot: number): BankItem \| null` | Get bank item by slot number (bank must be open). |
| `findBankItem(pattern: string \| RegExp): BankItem \| null` | Find bank item by name pattern (bank must be open; shortest matching name wins). |
| `getBankItems(): BankItem[]` | Get all bank items (bank must be open). |
| `isBankOpen(): boolean` | Check if bank interface is open. |
| `getNearbyNpc(index: number): NearbyNpc \| null` | Get NPC by index. |
| `findNearbyNpc(pattern: string \| RegExp, options?: FindOptions): NearbyNpc \| null` | Find NPC by name pattern (shortest matching name wins, then nearest; reachable preferred). |
| `getNearbyNpcs(): NearbyNpc[]` | Get all nearby NPCs. |
| `findNearbyPlayer(pattern: string \| RegExp, options?: FindOptions): NearbyPlayer \| null` | Find a nearby player by name pattern (shortest matching name wins, then nearest; reachable preferred). |
| `getNearbyPlayers(): NearbyPlayer[]` | Get all nearby players, nearest first. |
